**L629** `static lv_obj_t *ui_back_button(lv_obj_t *root, int ring_shown)`

~~~text
Back on Now Playing, which is not built on the header: the same button, in the same place where the layout allows.
A theme that hides the seek ring (terminal, bauhaus, zine) leaves the left edge free, so there it sits on the edge
like on every other screen (reach +8 px, to a 38 px target; the shuffle key starts at x 40). Where the ring runs
round the rim the edge is the ring itself, so Back takes the top-left corner inside it: 40 x 40 at 66,58, clear of
the cover (from x 106), of the shuffle key (from y 126) and of the top pull-down zone (y < 40), its glyph within
r 151 of the centre (the thickest ring, stone's, starts at r 154). Created after the theme's layout and before the
full-screen art overlay: above the controls, below the overlays. A swipe that starts on it does not also tap it
(ui_on drops a click that travelled), and the main loop's back swipe is unchanged.
~~~

**L1420** `static void update_cover_for_path(const track_state_t *st)`

~~~text
Two independent state pieces: last_path owns local decoding/display; the token,
generation and pending flag own the title-dependent online request.
Invariant: a title ready on the first snapshot (non-Opus, CUE/SACD,
streams) preserves the pre-Opus PATH lifecycle exactly: same path means
no restart, loading state or refetch. Only a pending identity adds work:
local/path work starts immediately; netart_* waits for its committed title
and is submitted once for that playback identity after a local miss.

path    identity    title             local/decode       action
changed any         ready (even empty) any                normal path request
changed any         pending           any                local only; arm online
same    changed     ready (even empty) any                keep path; disarm online
same    changed     pending           any                keep path; arm new identity
same    same        pending           any                wait for commitment
same    same        committed         running/unconsumed wait for local result
same    same        committed         present/cancelled  disarm; keep cover
same    same        committed         absent             disarm; online only once
Commitment before/after decode uses the same consumed-result barrier.
Empty ready titles retain netart's existing artist/album fallbacks.
~~~

## ui/usbhid.c

**L1** `#include "usbhid.h"`

~~~text
USB Audio media buttons. In USB Audio the Disc is the USB host and the IEM/DAC's play/next/volume buttons arrive
as a plain HID consumer-control device, which the kernel (usbhid + hid-generic) exposes as an evdev node. The
player only knows its own hardware keys, so diskOS reads those nodes itself and drives the same commands the
UI uses. Read-only (never EVIOCGRAB), opened only while the output route is USB, and event0/event1 (the Disc's
own keys and touch) are never touched: a node must resolve to a sysfs path containing "/usb". A press never
wakes a blanked panel (player-originated events must not call ui_backlight()); it only counts as activity.

Click gestures. Most single-button IEMs and DAC dongles send only the play/pause key, so that key is counted instead
of acted on at once (clicks.c): 1 click = play/pause, 2 = next, 3 = previous. A click sequence ends when 350 ms pass
after the last click (CLICKS_WINDOW_MS), or at once on the third click, so a single click's play/pause lands ~350 ms
late, as on any headset. Dedicated next / previous / volume keys are not counted and act immediately as before. The
play/pause key's debounce is 40 ms (CLICK_DEBOUNCE_MS) rather than 150 ms, or a quick triple click would lose clicks.
A pending sequence is dropped when the route leaves USB or the charge screen / keyboard is up. The window and the
2- and 3-click actions are fixed, not settings. Unverified on the JA11: which key code its button sends; usbhid logs
every action as "usbhid: eventN key C -> ...", so check that log first if a button does nothing.
~~~

~~~text
VOL_MAX is 120 (the player's 0715 scale); 2 = ~1.7% per press, 60 presses end to end
~~~

## ui/wifi.c

**L28** `#define WCLI "/usr/sbin/wpa_cli -i wlan0 "`

~~~text
Wi-Fi settings (SCR_WIFI) + a details screen (SCR_WIFI_INFO).

wpa_supplicant + udhcpc).  Scan/connect drive the running supplicant via
`wpa_cli -i wlan0`.  Connecting writes the network in and `save_config`s it
to /usr/data/wpa_supplicant.conf (update_config=1), so it persists.
Round-screen-aware: the top corners stay clear (only back chevron + centred
title); the on/off switch + scan button share one row in the wide centre
band.  The list itself carries state (connected checkmark row / "Wi-Fi is off" /
"Scanning" / "No networks") so there is no redundant status line.
NB: connecting to a DIFFERENT AP drops the laptop deploy link - recover over
serial if needed.
~~~


**L182** `#define RECO_SETTLE_MS 9000`

~~~text
Keepalive: whenever Wi-Fi should be on but wpa_supplicant isn't running (died, never
started, radio glitch) (re)start it, so a known network returning in range auto-joins.
Sanitize saved nets once the supplicant is up after each (re)launch - driven by a pending
flag (set on first run + every launch we initiate, cleared after one run), so it's
deterministic and idempotent regardless of pid reuse or a transient pidof miss. Enforce a
deliberate OFF against a late in-flight wifi_up. Self-rate-limited: safe to call each loop.
~~~

**L182** `#define RECO_SETTLE_MS 9000`

~~~text
---- V2.57 radio reconciliation ---------------------------------------------------------------------
V2.57's player turns Wi-Fi off at boot when both radios were saved on (keeps Bluetooth, saves WIFI_STATUS=0).
diskOS keeps its own "wifi_on" intent, and the keepalive below would restart Wi-Fi at once, undoing stock's
decision and leaving both radios fighting. So on firmware with that arbitration, each player generation (boot or
player restart) holds the keepalive until the player has answered and settled, then accepts stock's decision
ONLY for its exact signature. An explicit user choice at any point ends the hold and always wins; a player that
never answers releases the hold unchanged after RECO_GIVEUP_MS, so Wi-Fi cannot get stuck off.
~~~

~~~text
same settle as the local-init handshake (past the ~7 s mode-control window)
~~~


**L653** `static void wpa_q(const char *v, char *out, int cap){`

~~~text
Shell-safe token for a password: wpa_supplicant's quoted-string parser (wpa_config_parse_psk, 2.9)
takes the bytes between the first and LAST double quote literally, with no unescaping, and the
SET_NETWORK control command hands the rest of the line over untouched. So the value goes in as
"<bytes>" with NO backslash escaping (escaping " or \ would put a real backslash in the key); the
whole token is wrapped in shell single-quotes with any ' emitted as '\''. Output e.g. '"pa"ss\'
~~~

**L1007** `#define WNET_NO_RSSI (-1000)`

~~~text
Parse `wpa_cli scan_results` (bssid \t freq \t signal \t flags \t ssid) into out[] (max WNET_MAX).
SSIDs are printf-encoded by wpa_cli and are decoded to real bytes first (wifi_ssid_decode), so names
compare, dedupe, display and connect as what they are; undecodable/over-long/hidden rows are skipped.
Only newline-terminated rows count: a capture cut off mid-row (buffer full) loses its last row rather
than showing a partial name. Access points with the same SSID collapse into one row at the first
one's position, showing the strongest signal (duplicates are merged BEFORE the row cap applies).
The connected network (cur, may be "") is always row 0; the rest keep scan order. If cur is not in the
scan it is still shown first, using cur_rssi (dBm or WNET_NO_RSSI -> weakest bars) and cur_secured.
~~~

**L1116** `static void wifi_set_intent(int on){ cfg_set_int("wifi_on", on); }`

~~~text
wifi_up.sh runs async, so wpa_supplicant isn't up the instant the switch flips.
Show "Turning on Wi-Fi..." and poll until the radio is actually up before
scanning (otherwise start_scan() would immediately report "Wi-Fi is off").
The intent / bring-up watch / off teardown / toggle lifecycle is radio.c's; this is its Wi-Fi adapter, facts only.
Where it differs from Bluetooth: a timeout only reports (RADIO_REPORT_ONLY: the intent stays on and the keepalive
retries); the Quick Settings tile flips the persisted intent (that is what the tile shows); and a tile toggle does
not watch the bring-up (no Wi-Fi screen is waiting, and the keepalive enforces the intent).
~~~

## Notes on the strip

- **Python docstrings are not comments** and were left in place (306 of them, in 67 files). Only `#` comments moved here.
- **`ui/rmguard.c`** embeds a copy of `payload/diskos-rmguard` in `RMGUARD_SCRIPT` and the guard test compares the two byte for byte. The shell comments were removed from both, so the `payload/diskos-rmguard` entries above are also the comments of that embedded script.
- **`payload/S97diskos_install`** had `# >>> SUPERVISOR BEGIN` / `# <<< SUPERVISOR END` marker comments that `tests/test_boot_select.py` and `tests/test_sd_guards.py` sliced on. Those tests now slice from the supervisor's first statement (`if [ "$1" != "__worker" ]; then`) to the first statement after it (`SIGS="TERM HUP INT`).
- **Other test edits**: `ui/tests/boot_probe_test.py` (the `PDEATH` anchor line quoted a trailing comment) and `tests/test_windows_cli.py` (the expected PowerShell block quoted a comment line).
- **Kept as tool directives**: `# shellcheck disable=SC2046` (`build/build-windows-tools.sh`), `# noqa: E402` (four test files), `/* NOLINT */` (`ui/art.c`), `/* fall through */` (`ui/theme_kits.c`, read by GCC's `-Wimplicit-fallthrough`).
- **Makefiles**: GNU make keeps the blanks before a trailing `#` comment as part of a variable's value; those blanks went with the comment.
- **Verification**: Python files compare equal by AST, shell scripts by `bash --pretty-print`, C files by the `clang -E -P` token stream, Makefiles by `make -pnq`. A rebuild of `ui/mq_ui` from the stripped sources, made before the `RMGUARD_SCRIPT` edit, was byte-identical to the binary flashed on 2026-10-30.
